cells.v: dots.tts MeanFlow distillation at q8_0, served by audio.cpp rather than crispasr. The same 2B model the dots-tts row measures as SOAR. Against dots-soar-acpp, which holds runtime and precision fixed, the distillation is 1.16x SLOWER at n=3. The entire gap to the crispasr row is the runtime and the quantisation, worth 3.6x between them; the distillation contributes none of it here.

The SOAR checkpoint again, at q8_0 through audio.cpp instead of f16 through crispasr, as a control for the MeanFlow comparison. Same weights as the dots-tts row and 3.6x faster at n=3, which is the entire gap the MeanFlow row appeared to open. Against this control the distillation is 1.16x slower, not 3.3x faster: the single-pass version of this comparison had the sign wrong.

cells.v: Smallest of six published quantisations at 516 MB. Autoregressive despite the size: the GGUF declares a causal decoder with a codebook refinement head, and syntheses vary run to run. Across four free-seed runs the six variants span 6.0-7.0% mean WER, and the ordering changes between runs, so the ladder is not separable - precision buys memory, not accuracy.

cells.v: LFM2 backbone over NVIDIA's NeMo nano codec, 15 baked speakers. PESQ 3.86 against 10% WER - it sounds better than it transcribes, though zonos and melotts split wider still. Across three passes its mean WER moved 11.4%, 9.9%, 8.8%, so a single run would have placed it four rows lower. Runs on CPU because the published package never received the MPS fix its own examples carry; MPS measures about 8% slower anyway at this size, and fails about one generation in six.
